issues.legal_issue: A review is warranted where the prior judgment contains an error apparent on the face of the record that materially affects its reasoning.

When an agreement for specific performance does not fix a date for completing performance, limitation under Article 54 of the Limitation Act begins when the plaintiff has notice that performance has been refused.

A contractual period for payment of the balance consideration does not, without more, fix a date for completing performance where the agreement also conditions performance on the vendors furnishing documents and prescribes no such completion date.

A purchaser who has paid a substantial part of the consideration and is not required to tender the balance unless directed by the court may establish readiness and willingness under Section 16(c) of the Specific Relief Act.

Specific performance may be granted under the unamended Section 10 of the Specific Relief Act where compensation is presumed inadequate for breach of a contract to transfer immovable property and the agreement does not rebut that presumption.

The doctrine of lis pendens applies from institution of review proceedings, even while the petition remains defective in the registry, and binds a transferee of the disputed property to the outcome of the proceedings.
